topics.title: AngularJS Core Directives
topics.keyConcept: Directives are markers on DOM elements that extend HTML with custom behaviors. Key structural directives include ng-repeat, ng-if, and ng-show.
topics.content:
Directives are markers on DOM elements (like attributes, element names, or CSS classes) that tell AngularJS's HTML compiler ($compile) to attach custom behaviors or transform the DOM elements. Core directives include:

  • ng-repeat: Clones HTML elements for each item in a collection. It acts like a foreach loop: 
    <ul>
  <li ng-repeat="student in students | orderBy:'name'">
    {{ student.name }} (Roll: {{ student.roll }})
  </li>
</ul>
  • ng-if: Conditionally includes or excludes DOM elements. If false, the element is physically deleted from the DOM.
  • ng-show & ng-hide: Conditionally toggle CSS visibility styles (display: none) without removing the elements from the DOM tree.

Real-World Project Example: Admin dashboards. A list of logged-in users is rendered dynamically using ng-repeat. Delete buttons are rendered using ng-if="user.role === 'admin'", ensuring standard users do not see or load the button nodes in their browser DOM.
topics.commonMistakes: Confusing `ng-if` and `ng-show`. `ng-if` is resource-heavy because it continuously mounts/destroys DOM elements and scope variables. `ng-show` simply toggles CSS visibility, which is much faster for frequent toggle switches. Use `ng-show` for elements that toggle frequently (like tabs or dropdowns) and `ng-if` for static conditional sections.
topics.interviewTip: A common interview question is: `ng-if` vs `ng-show`. Explain that `ng-if` physically removes/creates elements in the DOM (higher performance cost for toggling, but lower memory overhead), while `ng-show` simply toggles the element's CSS visibility (faster toggling, but element remains in DOM).

topics.title: Controllers & Scope Inheritance
topics.keyConcept: Controllers manage component scope. Nested controllers establish prototypal scope inheritance, climbing up the chain to $rootScope.
topics.content:
Controllers: AngularJS controllers are JavaScript constructor functions that govern the data flow and user interaction for specific DOM regions. They are defined using the controller() module API and bind data/methods to the injected $scope object.

Nested Controllers & Prototypal Scope Inheritance: In AngularJS, controllers can be nested inside the HTML structure. Each controller creates its own scope instance. These scopes inherit prototypically from their parent controllers. If a property is read in the child scope, the JavaScript engine looks for it locally; if missing, it climbs up the parent scope chain until it reaches the global $rootScope at the top of the application.

// HTML View:
<div ng-controller="ParentCtrl">
  <p>Parent Value: {{ value }}</p>
  <div ng-controller="ChildCtrl">
    <p>Child Accessing Parent: {{ value }}</p>
  </div>
</div>

// JS Controller:
app.controller('ParentCtrl', function($scope) {
  $scope.value = 'Hello from Parent';
});
app.controller('ChildCtrl', function($scope) {
  // empty controller, inherits $scope.value prototypically
});
topics.commonMistakes: Modifying primitive scope variables (strings, numbers, booleans) inside nested child controllers. Prototypal inheritance creates a local copy (shadows) of primitives on the child scope instead of modifying the parent. Best practice is to bind data to objects: use a dot, like `$scope.data.value`, which preserves references.

topics.title: Built-in & Custom Filters
topics.keyConcept: Filters format data directly in HTML views using the pipe syntax |. Custom filters are created as modules returning formatter functions.
topics.content:
Filters format data for display in expressions without mutating the underlying model data. They are chained in views using the pipe symbol |:

  • currency: Formats numbers into currency format (e.g., {{ total | currency:'INR ' }}).
  • uppercase / lowercase: Standardizes string case formats.
  • orderBy: Sorts arrays based on object properties (e.g., {{ users | orderBy:'age' }}).
  • filter: Evaluates a subset of items from an array matching a search query.

Custom Filters: You can define custom filters to execute custom formatting logic (e.g., reversing text, masking digits):

// Define Custom Filter:
app.filter('maskEmail', function() {
  return function(email) {
    if (!email || !email.includes('@')) return email;
    const parts = email.split('@');
    const name = parts[0];
    const maskedName = name.substring(0, 2) + '****';
    return maskedName + '@' + parts[1];
  };
});

// Use in HTML:
<p>Masked: {{ user.email | maskEmail }}</p>
topics.commonMistakes: Chaining heavy filter operations inside large `ng-repeat` loops. Because filters are evaluated on every digestion cycle, running complex operations (like deep sorting or regex matches) on hundreds of items slows down UI interaction.

topics.title: Form Events & Custom Validations
topics.keyConcept: AngularJS intercepts HTML form submits using ng-submit, managing inputs state (valid, invalid, dirty, pristine) automatically.
topics.content:
AngularJS provides specialized directives to capture user inputs and handle form validations:

  • Event Directives: Directives like ng-click, ng-submit, ng-change, and ng-blur map DOM events directly to scope controller functions without manual listeners.
  • Form Validation State: AngularJS automatically tracks form input states, assigning CSS helper classes to the form based on validation rules:
    • $valid: True if all inputs pass validation rules.
    • $invalid: True if any input fails a rule.
    • $dirty: True if the user has interacted with the input.
    • $pristine: True if the input has not been touched yet.

Form Event Validation Example:

<form name="userForm" ng-submit="submitForm(userForm.$valid)" novalidate>
  <input type="email" name="email" ng-model="user.email" required />
  <span ng-show="userForm.email.$dirty && userForm.email.$invalid">Valid email required.</span>
  <button type="submit" ng-disabled="userForm.$invalid">Register</button>
</form>
topics.commonMistakes: Forgetting to add the `novalidate` attribute to the `<form>` element. Without `novalidate`, the browser's default native HTML5 validation will trigger, overriding AngularJS's custom error messages and disabling states.

topics.title: Services & Dependency Injection
topics.keyConcept: Services are singleton objects holding reusable logic, injected into controllers as parameter dependencies resolved by the DI engine.
topics.content:
Services: AngularJS services are singleton objects containing reusable business logic, calculations, and data sharing modules. They are instantiated lazily on demand. Core services include:

  • $http: Performs asynchronous AJAX calls to fetch or submit data to backend servers.
  • $timeout & $interval: Wrappers for window timeouts that trigger digestion cycles automatically to update the view.

Dependency Injection (DI): AngularJS implements DI to pass dependencies to controllers. Instead of manually instantiating services using the `new` keyword, you declare the service names as arguments in your controller constructor, and AngularJS's injector resolves them:

// Controller with Injected Services ($scope, $http, $timeout):
app.controller('ProductController', function($scope, $http, $timeout) {
  $scope.products = [];
  $scope.loading = true;

  $http.get('https://api.example.com/products')
    .then(function(response) {
      $scope.products = response.data;
      $timeout(function() {
        $scope.loading = false;
      }, 1000);
    })
    .catch(function(error) {
      console.error('Failed to load products:', error);
    });
});
topics.commonMistakes: Losing dependency references during minification. When code is minified, argument names like `($scope, $http)` are renamed to shorter names like `(a, b)`, breaking the DI matching. Avoid this by using the inline array annotation: `app.controller('ProductController', ['$scope', '$http', function($scope, $http) { ... }]);`.

practiceQuestions.question: Explain the difference between the ng-if and ng-show directives in AngularJS.
practiceQuestions.answer: `ng-if` conditionally adds or removes elements from the DOM entirely based on a boolean value. `ng-show` (and `ng-hide`) does not modify the DOM structure; it toggles the CSS `display` property (`display: block` or `display: none`) to show or hide the element.

practiceQuestions.question: How does scope inheritance work with nested controllers in AngularJS?
practiceQuestions.answer: AngularJS scopes inherit prototypally. If you nest HTML elements containing different controllers, the inner (child) controller's scope will inherit all properties and methods defined on the outer (parent) controller's scope. If the child controller modifies a primitive variable, it shadow-copies it locally, unless objects are utilized.

practiceQuestions.question: What are AngularJS filters? Give examples of three built-in filters.
practiceQuestions.answer:
Filters are formatting utilities used in views to modify data before rendering. Examples:
(1) `uppercase`: `{{ 'test' | uppercase }}` output: TEST
(2) `currency`: `{{ 50 | currency }}` output: $50.00
(3) `orderBy`: `ng-repeat="user in users | orderBy:'age'"` sorts users by age.

practiceQuestions.question: What is Dependency Injection (DI) and how is it used in AngularJS controllers?
practiceQuestions.answer: Dependency Injection is a design pattern where an object receives its dependencies from an external system rather than creating them itself. In AngularJS, controllers declare their dependencies (such as `$scope` or `$http`) as function parameters, and the AngularJS framework automatically resolves and injects them at runtime.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the built-in $http service in AngularJS? Provide a usage example.

mcqs.question: Which AngularJS directive acts like a loop to iterate over an array of items?
mcqs.explanation: The `ng-repeat` directive instantiates a template block for each item in an array.

mcqs.question: What is the difference between ng-if and ng-show?
options: ng-if hides via CSS, ng-show removes from DOM
ng-if removes the element from the DOM, while ng-show toggles its CSS display property
They do the exact same thing
ng-if only works on text, ng-show works on divs
mcqs.explanation: ng-if completely adds/deletes nodes from the DOM tree, whereas ng-show modifies the CSS display property.

mcqs.question: Which filter is used in an expression to format a number as cash?
mcqs.explanation: The `currency` filter formats a numeric value into currency format (defaults to dollars, but customizable).

mcqs.question: How are filters applied inside AngularJS expressions?
mcqs.explanation: AngularJS uses the pipe symbol `|` to chain filters inside expressions.

mcqs.question: Which built-in AngularJS service is used to make AJAX requests to a server?
mcqs.explanation: The `$http` service is the core AngularJS service for communicating with remote HTTP endpoints.

mcqs.question: What is the mechanism by which AngularJS controllers receive dependent services at runtime?
mcqs.explanation: AngularJS uses Dependency Injection (DI) to pass requested services as parameters to controllers during startup.

mcqs.question: The topmost scope in an AngularJS application is called what?
mcqs.explanation: The `$rootScope` is the parent of all other scopes created in the application, associated with the element containing `ng-app`.

mcqs.question: Built-in AngularJS services are prefixed with which character?
mcqs.explanation: AngularJS prefixes all built-in services (e.g. `$http`, `$timeout`, `$route`) with a dollar sign `$` to avoid naming collisions with custom variables.

mcqs.question: Which directive can bind a click handler function to a button in AngularJS?
mcqs.explanation: The `ng-click` directive tells AngularJS to execute a custom scope function when that element is clicked.

mcqs.question: If a nested child controller scope modifies a variable, which mechanism is used to resolve properties?
mcqs.explanation: Scope inheritance is built on top of prototypal inheritance, checking properties up the parent scope chain.
